# Independent proactive visual QA — issue #72

Issue: [Supply permitted playable media with explicit timeline and generation annotations](https://github.com/dystrophyless/dubbed.ai/issues/72). Reviewer: **GPT-6.1 Sol, High**. Review date: 2026-10-25, Windows, local mock environment. Dedicated scope: issue #72 only. Verdict: the narrow corpus identity/playability contract is supported in fresh Chromium; **one MEDIUM requirement/design coverage flaw and one LOW optional diagnostic improvement** remain. No confirmed implementation defect or production-rendering claim is made.

## Snapshot and purpose

Code HEAD: `9d286621177200fdb5f61ef963d0b6818ae76774`. The pre-existing dirty documentation, skills and evidence tree was preserved. `git diff --numstat -- frontend/public/media frontend/src/media/fixtures.ts frontend/tests/media` returned no changes. Current local flow documents were read as the current requirements, including the later 1.000–120.000-second selection policy; historical acceptance wording about unresolved minimum policy is not treated as current product policy. The supplied live issue snapshot is closed with zero comments. No GitHub mutation, product/spec edit, commit or push occurred.

This is a nonvisual foundation task with no standalone screen. Its user job is to give downstream developers/reviewers reliable, permitted local media, exact expected turn placement and unmistakable output identities. Visible consequences were reviewed through real New dub → Record → Result screens and native playback. Those screens remain owned by their respective issues; observations here do not reopen or accept those tasks.

## Fresh evidence and method

Own Vite process: `npm.cmd run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4372 --strictPort` from `frontend`. Isolated Playwright Chromium context, actual installed browser version in [metrics.json](metrics.json), DPR 1, headless, `--mute-audio`, fake-device/fake-UI flags and microphone permission. Audio output stayed muted at the browser process level even when application media elements reported `muted:false`. No physical microphone or speakers were used. Screenshots were captured after `document.fonts.ready`; every PNG listed below was opened and visually inspected. All product screenshots are full-page captures; viewport dimensions describe the initial viewport, not the expanded image height.

UI journey: changed locale through visible controls; registered a unique `example.test` local mock account using the visible simulated code; uploaded actual `source-dialogue.mp4`; requested the exact 9-credit quote; processed; connected the fake microphone; captured and accepted three fake-device takes through visible actions; downloaded the displayed result. No backend, seeded project, alternate product service, or real email was used. The separate generation comparison is explicitly reviewer-authored diagnostic HTML with native players, **not a product screen**.

Executed targeted command: `node --test frontend/tests/media/fixtures.test.mjs` — **PASS 3/3** at this dirty-worktree boundary. This checks all 13 actual asset hashes/byte lengths, generated timeline arithmetic, zeroed PCM, absent-data sentinel, generation distinctness and stored observation annotations. Historical browser observations inside the manifest are not a new cross-browser run.

Fresh actual-file native playback probe: source, generation 001, generation 002, silence MP4, usable partial, video-only and short source all reached `ended` in Chromium at 4× playback while muted. Durations: 8.6254, 8.6157, 8.649867, 1.992233, 2.7989, 1.194133 and 0.646867 seconds respectively. See [capture.log](capture.log) and [metrics.json](metrics.json). Downloaded generation 001: 211221 bytes, SHA-256 `af77d8889ab4675a7b70f28955930ee7cf094f2c9f07452b60da26522ddf87a2`, exactly matching the manifest. The downloaded name `source-dialogue.mp4` is a project-derived filename; byte identity, not the filename, proves generation identity.

| AC-02 playback and identity | Actual measured playback; exact known timeline; different result identities | Seven MP4s reach ended; generation 001 download matches hash; both generation title cards/colors differ visibly. | Supported in current desktop Chromium only. |
| AC-02 timeline annotations | Exact PCM placements with explicit limits | Three known quotes at 1000–2934.2857, 1500–3399.2290 and 5000–6714.2404ms; intentional overlap 1500–2934.2857ms. Manifest explicitly distinguishes PCM placement from decoded MP4/product timing. | Source/test supported; no listening or synchronization accuracy certification. |
| AC-03 silence / usable partial / no data | Distinct truth; no invented duration rejection | Separate zeroed PCM/audio-track silence, clean simulated partial marked `representsRealInterruptionRecovery:false`, null/absent noData; source minimum policy is separate. | Supported; actual interruption/finalization recovery unproved by this fixture. |
| AC-04 local-only / no implicit demo | Backend-free local assets; no prepopulated sample project | Fresh account began New dub; source/result appeared only after explicit upload/processing/recording. Result EN/RU states it is synthetic, not assembled from accepted takes/custom upload. | Supported in sampled journey; no landing demo observed. |
| EN desktop 1440×900; short 1440×700 | Readable fixture identity and controls | No horizontal overflow; Mabry loaded; result/source identity readable. | Observed, with small desktop controls noted below. |
| RU phone 390×844 | Fit viewport and preserve synthetic truth | No horizontal overflow; 48px/16px primary action; Russian result disclaimer visible. Recorded dialogue stays English because the source fixture is English, not an untranslated UI label. | Observed; real mobile media stack untested. |

## Findings

### QA-72-01 — MEDIUM — Minimal title-card corpus cannot challenge the real scene / orientation experience

**Classification:** requirement/design coverage flaw, confirmed corpus limitation; **not a proven runtime bug or violation of an explicit portrait-fixture AC**. Related: AC-02 and consuming Flow09 purpose / Flow10 orientation preservation. The issue deliberately asks for a compact mechanical corpus but does not require representative visual scene stress; that makes its acceptance too narrow to support later visual-readiness conclusions.

**Reproduce:** upload the bundled source; process and enter Record at desktop and phone; finish the three lines and open Result. Compare all MP4 definitions at `frontend/tests/media/generate-fixtures.mjs:381–388`: every video is 16:9, either 640×360 or 320×180; the largest playable source is approximately 8.6 seconds. `draw` at lines 213–225 draws a background, moving stripe and a permanent title, with no character/scene detail.

**Expected for convincing downstream visual QA:** at least one permitted portrait scene-like source and an annotated representative longer/long-dialogue case that can expose cropping, real subject visibility and recording-reading load. **Actual:** large sparse title cards remain trivially legible and the three short sentences are unusually easy to fit. The corpus proves file identity well, but does not test whether a user can recognize the active speaker, follow a scene, read a long line, or keep a portrait subject visible. Approved Flow10 line 13 requires orientation preservation; current fixtures never challenge it. No claim is made that the app currently crops portrait media incorrectly.

**Impact:** downstream screenshot acceptance can overestimate visual usability by seeing a highly forgiving, landscape-only stimulus. The risk is material for a media-first recording product, even while this issue's minimal corpus follows its original AC.

**Scoped recommendation / next validation:** keep these compact identity fixtures; add one original/generated portrait scene with recognizable subjects and timed turn markers, plus one representative long-line/longer-selection case. Explicitly require downstream visual gates to use them. Capture the same source/Record/Result states at desktop, short height and phone; inspect subject containment, long-dialogue readability and control access. Do not claim natural dubbing quality from that synthetic addition.

Evidence: source and Record show only the easy title stimulus; RU phone has a single short English sentence. These are fresh product screens:

![Source preview — EN desktop](evidence/source-en-desktop.png)

![Record — EN desktop](evidence/record-en-desktop.png)

![Record — RU phone](evidence/record-ru-phone.png)

### QA-72-02 — LOW — Exact timeline is machine-readable but the video lacks a visual timing oracle

**Classification:** optional fixture diagnostic improvement, confirmed observation; not an AC failure. Related: AC-02 exact timeline / overlap / generation annotations.

**Reproduce:** seek/play the source across the first two intentionally overlapping turns. Manifest `frontend/public/media/fixture-manifest.json:1399–1439` provides precise frame/sample offsets, but video drawing `generate-fixtures.mjs:213–225` displays only the generic label and moving stripe. The stripe position is not a labeled clock or documented turn boundary. The quotes “A blue light is on”, “I hear it clearly”, “We can begin now” are intentionally short, arbitrary English test utterances; neither their meaning nor the title card identifies the current speaker visually.

**Expected improvement / actual:** reviewers debugging a muted timing capture would benefit from burned-in frame/time and turn IDs. Current images can prove the synthetic source or generation identity, but cannot locate the exact annotated speech event. This report therefore uses metadata/test evidence for offsets and makes no screenshot-based timing claim.

**Impact:** silent review and failure triage require extra manifest/audio tooling; an apparent synchronization problem cannot be separated visually from an intentionally overlapping turn.

**Scoped recommendation / next validation:** add a clearly labeled fixture clock and separate turn-A/turn-B indicators to a diagnostic asset (retain old hashes until an intentional corpus revision). Test indicator transitions against the same PCM placement data and inspect known frames before/inside/after overlap. Keep “synthetic” and generation identifiers visible; do not add product subtitles or imply that this is product-rendered output.

The two real generation files are visibly distinct. This screenshot is a reviewer-authored diagnostic surface, not Dubbed UI:

![Actual generation fixtures in native players — diagnostic only](evidence/generations-native-probe.png)

## What works, and desktop control critique

The corpus uses obvious synthetic titles and different generation colors/labels, and the product repeats a localized synthetic-result disclaimer beside the generation. This avoids pretending the three fake-device takes generated the supplied output. The visible turn text matches the manifest quote. The exact source duration shown in New dub (8.625 seconds) is browser-derived, rather than blindly presenting the 8.650-second requested recorder window.

The adopted button reference was read at `_docs/evidence/affect-ui-clean-light/source/components/button/Clean/button-clean.md.txt:289–388` and its matching Light `01-initial.png` visually inspected. It establishes 28px / 13px desktop defaults, while the product retains Mabry. Native players/waveforms have no direct Affect source component; this review makes no source-exact player fidelity claim.

Measured actual desktop `Record line`: **110.55×28px, 13px Mabry**. `Download MP4`: **133.25×28px, 13px**. Phone equivalents: **175×48px and 358×48px, 16px**. The desktop source alignment is intentional, but 28px is still a small repeated recording action; the sparse fixture scene makes it especially apparent that more comfortable 36–40px primary recording geometry could fit. This is a **consumer/shared-control design concern**, not a #72 fixture defect and not asserted as an accessibility violation. A targeted future usability comparison should measure click misses and repeated-turn comfort with a realistic scene/long line; source approval alone does not settle that question.

At 1440×700 the Record action begins around y=656 and the volume/status below it require scrolling. Full-page capture below is not proof they fit within 700px. The phone pinned controls remain readable, but the fixture's short line is not a long-dialogue/keyboard-occlusion stress case.

![Record — short EN desktop viewport](evidence/record-en-short.png)

![Result — EN desktop](evidence/result-en-desktop.png)

![Result — RU phone](evidence/result-ru-phone.png)

## Limitations and coverage gaps

No real listening, loudspeaker output, physical microphone, lip/voice synchronization, codec frame-time certification, real interruption recovery, AI separation/rendering, production compatibility or legal review. Fresh playback covered current Chromium only, not fresh Firefox/WebKit/Safari/iOS/Android. The manifest's 2026-10-23 cross-engine facts—including Firefox timeouts and WebKit duration discrepancies—remain historical and are not converted into current PASS claims. The fresh generation-002 proof is native actual-file playback and a diagnostic screenshot; updated-generation handoff/Watch new was not rerun through UI. The result is visibly synthetic and cannot prove accepted-take mixing.

Not run: full suite/build/lint, 767/768 breakpoint matrix, 200% zoom, all EN/RU viewport permutations, comprehensive focus/hover/dialog/loading/error matrix, and source-size/format policy boundary tests. Those are explicit bounded-review gaps, not silent passes. Actual silence/track truth was checked by the targeted existing asset test and manifest annotations; screenshot appearance alone cannot distinguish silence from absent audio. The clean simulated partial cannot establish malformed/truncated-container recovery.

Artifacts: [metrics](metrics.json), [capture log](capture.log), [capture script](capture.cjs), [generation diagnostic script](generations.cjs), and [screenshot manifest](screenshot-manifest.json). All seven PNGs are fresh and visually opened. No product fixes were made.
